system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer-side review

The Seller’s “FINAL” labels and assertions of market consensus do not alter Wattlebridge’s approved positions. The draft departs materially from the playbook and should not be accepted as settled.

### 1. Liability framework

| Issue | Seller position | Buyer position / pushback |
|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Reject. Start at 25% / AUD 6m. The 20% cap is only an authorised fallback with Amelia Frost’s prior written approval; none exists. |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | Reject. Reduce to AUD 5,000. |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, with recovery only above the basket | Reject. AUD 50,000 aggregate basket, with recovery from the first dollar once exceeded. |
| General claims period | 18 months | Reject. Require 24 months after Completion. |
| All-claims override | Limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded | Reject. This is a hidden general-regime override and could capture title, tax, IP, payment, covenant and indemnity claims. Categories must remain separate. |
| Fundamental/title claims | Same cap and time limits as general warranties | Reject entirely. Require a separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. |
| Fraud/misconduct | All limitations and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims | Reject. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. |

### 2. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

The proposed disclosure is materially overbroad:

- “Every fact, matter and circumstance” in the data room, public registers and statutory records is not specific fair disclosure.
- A prudent buyer should not be required to identify the relevant breach from an entire data room.
- The reservation that nothing admits breach or liability further weakens the purported disclosures.

Require disclosure against each relevant warranty with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its consequences. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

Delete the blanket exclusion for matters known by the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from records. If any knowledge qualifier remains, it must identify named Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. It must never apply to title, capacity, fraud, deliberate misconduct or specific indemnities.

### 3. Bluefen consent

This is a material customer concentration issue: approximately AUD 3.6m, or 30% of FY26 revenue. The Seller expressly confirms that:

- no final written consent has been provided; and
- no evidence shows that the conditions in clause 11.3 have been satisfied.

“Reasonable endeavours” and consent merely being delivered are insufficient. Completion should require:

1. effective Bluefen change-control consent; and  
2. documentary evidence that every condition to that consent has been satisfied or waived.

The SPA should also provide a termination, deferral or other buyer remedy if consent is not obtained. This should not be treated as a routine post-Completion matter.

### 4. Riverlark facility and security

Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding and no final security discharge is included. A release after Completion is unacceptable without adequate protection.

Require:

- a current payout figure;
- repayment directly from Completion funds;
- effective releases of all Riverlark security at or before Completion; and
- delivery of evidence of repayment and release.

If a post-Completion release is unavoidable, require an irrevocable undertaking, appropriate funds retention/security and Amelia Frost’s specific written approval. The Seller should not receive the relevant funds while its security remains in place.

### 5. Employee bonuses

DD-005 records AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses, yet the Seller confirms they are omitted from the funds flow. This creates an obvious risk that the Buyer pays the price and subsequently bears pre-Completion remuneration, payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.

Require the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs to be:

- separately itemised in the Completion funds flow;
- paid or funded by the Seller at Completion; and
- expressly treated as a Seller liability/pre-Completion leakage item.

The funds flow must not silently exclude them.

### 6. Ironquay IP

The specific indemnity is too narrow if it only covers the SOW3 payment. DD-004 says transfer of the Project Materials depends on payment of every SOW3 fee, while DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open and lacks independent verification.

Require a broader indemnity covering:

- all costs, claims and losses arising from failure to obtain ownership or usable rights in the Ironquay materials;
- any unpaid SOW3 amounts and related interest/costs;
- infringement or third-party claims; and
- remediation, replacement or re-development costs.

Preserve the SOW3 cure mechanism, but require proof of payment and effective transfer/assignment. The AUD 180,000 figure should not be treated as verified or as a cap on the exposure.

### 7. Export/privacy incident

DD-006 is unresolved, not immaterial merely because no loss has yet been quantified. The disclosure confirms an unintended external email, potential exposure of approximately 1,240 records and a preliminary investigation.

The SPA should require:

- preservation of logs and other evidence;
- continued investigation by appropriately qualified personnel;
- prompt written updates to the Buyer;
- cooperation with regulatory, customer and notification assessments;
- no destruction or alteration of relevant records; and
- a specific indemnity or expressly preserved warranty protection for resulting liabilities.

The drafting must not assume either a confirmed breach or no breach, notification duty, harm or numeric loss. The Buyer should preserve its rights pending factual determination.

### 8. Sandbar supplier renewals

The three renewals total AUD 330,000, but the disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, accrued, terminable or ordinary-course. The Seller’s assertion that they are ordinary-course is not enough.

Require the Buyer to assess the agreements and renewal mechanics. Do not automatically classify the amount as Debt or deduct it from price without analysis. Obtain termination, non-renewal, accrued-liability and timing information and ensure no pre-Completion obligation is improperly transferred to the Buyer.

### 9. Title and authority

DD-012 is an internal share register and is not independent proof of clean title. It does not establish absence of competing interests, encumbrances, adverse claims or authority defects.

Require independent evidence of:

- Harbourglass’s ownership of 100% of the shares;
- absence and release of all encumbrances;
- authority and capacity to sell;
- valid issuance and fully paid status of the shares; and
- completion of any required corporate or registry verification.

Title and capacity warranties must remain fundamental claims with the separate six-year/100% regime.

### 10. Tax and IP

The Seller’s statement that tax and IP are “settled” is unsupported by the supplied material and conflicts with the playbook. There is no approved resolution and no authority for unlimited liability or for subsuming these matters into the general regime.

Keep tax and IP terms open, separately negotiated and separately protected. Do not allow the general cap, basket, time limit, knowledge exclusion or exclusive-remedy language to override them unless expressly agreed by the Buyer.

### 11. Other disclosed contractual matters

The office lease and Mossvale disclosures should be checked against the underlying contracts. The Seller’s characterisation that they do not necessarily require consent is not determinative. Require confirmation of:

- whether the relevant provisions are triggered by the share sale or control change;
- whether notice, consent or waiver is required;
- whether any breach or termination right exists; and
- whether evidence of compliance is needed before Completion.

## Recommended negotiation position

1. Reject the Seller’s claim that the positions are final or already agreed.
2. Reinstate the Buyer’s general framework: 25% cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket and 24-month claims period.
3. Separate and strengthen fundamental/title, tax, IP, payment and covenant protections.
4. Insert comprehensive fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-outs.
5. Replace general disclosure and blanket knowledge provisions with specific fair disclosure and a tightly defined knowledge standard.
6. Make Bluefen consent and satisfaction of its conditions a Completion requirement.
7. Repay Riverlark directly from Completion funds and obtain effective security releases.
8. Fund and itemise all DD-005 bonuses and on-costs.
9. Broaden the Ironquay indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure.
10. Preserve evidence and ongoing protections for DD-006.
11. Investigate Sandbar, office lease and Mossvale matters rather than accepting the Seller’s conclusions.
12. Require independent title evidence and keep tax/IP negotiations open.
=== END ADVICE ===
